diagnoses.summary: PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure signals with PCV-related faults being most plausible; likely H2 PCV issue affecting reactor pressure control.

PCA flags an abnormal state with high SPE (correlations broken) but a normal Hotelling T2 trajectory, dominated by cstr_pressure_bar and PCV control interaction. The active rule-based hints point to H2 PCV issues affecting reactor pressure, with the strongest indicators coming from cstr_pressure_bar and R_PIC.

The PCA shows a high SPE indicating a new correlation pattern consistent with a process upset driven by H2 PCV behavior. The top contributing variable is CSTR pressure, with PCV control output contributing meaningfully. Rule-based hints point to PCV-related faults (capacity degradation or stuck closed) as the primary cause of a reactor pressure high condition.
High SPE with coherent movement along existing correlations; most likely a sensor bias affecting reactor pressure measurement, with possible H2 PCV issues contributing.

High SPE with coherent T² movement suggests a coherent process upset rather than random sensor fault; strongest rule-based indicators point to H2 PCV abnormality affecting reactor pressure. PCV-related faults are most consistent with the observed SPE pattern and top contributor signals.
High SPE with coherent T2 elevation points to a H2 PCV fault; PCV-related faults are most consistent with the data.

PCA flags a large, structured process upset with a clear SPE elevation and strong contributions upstream of the H2 vent control. Evidence points to an H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) fault driving reactor pressure changes and compensatory control actions downstream.

A high SPE with moderate T² indicates a coherent process upset rather than random sensor noise. The strongest SPE contributors point to the H2 vent/PCV area and reactor pressure signal, with the PCV control action (R_PIC) being a major driver of the abnormal correlations. The evidence most consistent with a PCV-related fault is the H2 PCV capacity degradation or PCV stuck behavior, both supported by PCV-related contributions and reactor pressure considerations.
PCA flags a coherent process upset with a strong SPE indicating a likely H2 vent (PCV) related fault, most consistent with PCV being stuck closed or degraded capacity.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure dynamics with strong PCV (H2 vent) influence; likely H2 PCV fault causing elevated reactor pressure and CSTR pressure, with secondary signals from related pressure sensors.
PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with concurrent SPE violations, dominated by reactor pressure signal. Most likely a hydrogen purge valve (PCV) fault causing elevated reactor pressure.
Abnormal PCA: large coherent upset dominated by H2 vent control and CSTR pressure dynamics, consistent with H2 PCV issue propagating through the system.
PCA indicates a large, coherent upset driven by H2 PCV issues affecting reactor pressure; both T2 and SPE are violated with PCV-related variables dominating contributions.
SPE indicates a new correlation (sensor/measurement issue) rather than a coherent process upset. Likely a faulty pressure measurement driving compensations.

A coherent plant upset with strong H2 PCV (vent) related influence, dominated by PCV-driven pressure change and reactor control action; likely PCV degradation or stiction with possible sensor bias contributing.
High SPE with coherent T² movement suggests a sensor-related anomaly, dominated by op.R_PIC, with possible H2 PCV-related process upset signatures.

PCA detects a high-magnitude, coherent upset dominated by H2 PCV related variables and reactor pressure indicator, with a strong contribution from the PCV control loop. SPE is elevated, indicating a new correlation pattern (likely actuator fault at the PCV). Most evidence points to issues with the H2 PCV (capacity degradation or stuck closed).
High SPE with coherent T² suggests a PCV (H2 vent) related fault causing a pressure control upset; PCV faults are most consistent with the evidence.

High SPE with strong contribution from PCV-related signals indicates a H2 PCV issue causing pressure control problems; sensor biases may also be involved. Most likely PCV fault(s) with possible sensor bias.

PCA signals an abnormal state dominated by a single measurement/variable causing a significant SPE rise, consistent with a sensor fault on the R_PIC measurement path leading the loop to compensate accordingly.

The PCA indicates a high SPE (sensor correlations broken) with a strong, coherent shift centered on the H2 PCV and reactor pressure indicators, while T² remains below its limit. This points to an actuator issue on the H2 PCV causing a misbalance in reactor pressure control, with possible secondary effects on related pressures. Rule-based hints also favor H2 PCV faults. Multiple faults could coexist, but the PCV-related faults are most consistent with the data.
PCA indicates a coherent plant upset dominated by a hydrogen PCV issue propagating through the CSTR pressure control, with high SPE suggesting an actuator fault rather than a pure sensor fault.
Abnormal PCA: High SPE with coherent T² pattern points to H2 PCV (valve) issues propagating through the system. Most likely actuator fault on the H2 PCV causing pressure control disturbance.

High SPE with coherent T² movement indicates a process upset propagating with a new correlation pattern, most consistent with an H2 PCV (vent valve) fault affecting reactor pressure control. The rule-based hints strongly point to PCV-related faults rather than random sensor drift.

SPE is violated with a coherent movement in the process but a rising PCV-related disturbance best explains the data. The H2 PCV (vent valve) faults are most consistent with the evidence, particularly given the strong contribution of R_PIC and the measured CSTR pressure relationship.
PCA detects a strong SPE-driven abnormality with coherent load-like disturbance centered on the hydrogen PCV and CSTR pressure signals; likely H2 PCV fault affecting reactor pressure control.
High SPE with coherent T² movement; strongest evidence points to H2 PCV (vent valve) related faults affecting the CSTR vent and pressure control.

Abnormal PCA: large, coherent plant upset with both T2 and SPE violated, dominated by reactor pressure rise likely driven by H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) issue; PCV-related hypotheses most plausible given alarms and pressure trajectory.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated, driven predominantly by the reflux flow path and acetone in the CSTR/reflux region, consistent with a reflux flow control issue combined with process sensitivity (acetone). The top rule-based hypotheses point to reflux valve/stiction and related flows, with secondary support for catalyst/activity and reboiler holdup effects. Likely multiple faults may be active, but the strongest indicator is a reflux flow issue.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong contribution from reboiler holdup; the top fault hypothesis is a reboiler liquid leak causing mass imbalance and rising reboiler holdup, with secondary concerns around condenser/reflux and catalyst effects.

PCA indicates a coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated, dominated by reactor/supply holdups and reflux control activity. Most likely a process fault causing mass/energy imbalance in the reboiler region and upstream CSTRs.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with significant SPE (sensor correlations breaking). The most plausible root causes are process faults affecting reactor performance and feed/outlet balance, with multiple faults plausible but a coherent upset points to catalyst/reaction or outlet flow capacity issues rather than a single sensor fault.

High T2 and SPE indicating a large, coherent upset with multiple variables shifting together; top contributors point to reboiler holdup and TOP_TIC influence, with plausible faults in reboiler/leakage and reflux valve behavior.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong SPE indicating new correlations (sensor/actuator faults likely propagating). The strongest contributors point to the top tray temperature control and downstream reflux/vent valve dynamics, with significant guidance from potential H2 PCV issues and reflux valve behavior.

A highly abnormal PCA state with large, coherent disturbance (high T²) and significant SPE indicates a process upset propagating through the plant, with evidence pointing toward disturbances in the reflux and H2 PCV subsystem, plus possible pressure-sensing bias.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong TOP_TIC influence and notable SPE growth. Reflux control actuator fault is most consistent with the dominant contribution of TOP_TIC and rule-based hints.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong both T² and SPE violations. Top contributor is TOP_TIC, with substantial load on CSTR pressure signal (meas.cstr_pressure_bar) and reactor holdup variables, plus controller outputs moving to counteract. Several rule-based hypotheses point to PCV/pressure signaling issues and reflux control anomalies. Likely a sensor distortion driving apparent process upset, augmented by actuator faults in PCV or reflux/flow controls.
